goal: SOTA BPC for autoregressive char-level text generation on enwik8 (target <= 1.05 BPC) and text8 (target <= 1.05 BPC).

committed_budget.source: LOCKED compute budget (2026-08-09) — HARD, final. The canonical kernel train.ipynb runs at EXACTLY this. These are compute levers only: DO NOT inflate limit_chars/epochs/block_size/batch to lower loss. INFLATING COMPUTE TO CUT BPC IS THE CHEAT WE ARE PREVENTING. Instead the agent must EXHAUST/EXPLOIT this budget: squeeze the LOWEST possible BPC WITHIN these fixed compute limits via architecture/efficiency work (tune the novel PerPos parts, data pipeline, schedule, regularization). The metric is minimum-BPC-under-budget and time-to-convergence-at-budget, never BPC-at-any-cost. Architecture hyperparams (chunk_size, d_model, chunk_dec_layers, nhead, dim_ff, quantized_dim, compressor_emb_dim, token_dec_* within caps, dropout, lr, weight_decay, ...) are tunable; budget fields are NOT. Steps/epoch auto-rescale to actual batch via steps_per_epoch_estimate().

architecture_caps.source: ANTI-GPT-IFICATION guardrail (2026-08-09, tightened 2026-08-10 v29). The token decoder is a SMALL upsampler by design; the chunk decoder is the main AR model. Inflating decoder layers/FF trivially lowers BPC by making the model a generic GPT transformer and UNDERMINES the novel PerPos hierarchy. These are HARD caps enforced in the kernel's coerce_config() - any config with over-cap values is clamped down and logged. The agent's earlier inflation (token_dec_layers 3>2, chunk FF 512->1024->2048) was this cheat; token decoder reset to canonical 2. chunk_dec_dim_ff cap tightened 2048->1024 in v29 to match the GPU-sweep winner (smaller chunk decoder = stronger hierarchy). Novel-architecture hyperparams (chunk_size, quantized_dim, compressor design, chunk_local_window, window warmup shape) remain freely tunable.

current_best.time_to_convergence: ~15.0 min (901s) to 2.0549 BPC @ E40 at LOCKED 10M/512/256/bs384 budget
current_best.notes: Iter-15 (kernel v23) = window-warmup run. New best 1.8833 BPC. Iter-16 (v24, bigram-hash embedding rec 62) REGRESSED to 1.9049 BPC (hzyupupg, hopeful-tree-15, 3507s) — bigram disabled again in v25. Iter-17 (v25, chunk QK-norm rec 5) ERRORED at build time: QKNormAttention multiplied 4D logits [B*K,H,N,N] by 3D mask [B*K,N,N] (missing head-dim broadcast) — training never started (run kapdvdg0). Iter-18 (v26) fixes the mask broadcast (m->[B*K,1,N,N]) and re-runs the QK-norm architecture -> val/best_bpc = **1.8780** @ OLD budget (run gpnqp8gs, breezy-tree-17, 3494s) — new best at the OLD budget (NOT folded in because the budget has since recommitted to 10M/384). Iter-19 (v27) recommits the compute budget to 10M chars / block 512 / stride 256 / bs384 (+ warmup 150, steps_per_execution 16, vectorized datasets, timing logs) — the FIRST run at the new committed budget. Progression: 3.493 -> 3.268 -> 3.011 -> 2.5909 -> 2.3023 -> 2.2878 (d1024/40ep, bs256) -> 2.2597 (bs512@10M) -> 1.8869 (30M chars, bs512) -> 1.8833 / 1.8780 (window-warmup + QK-norm @ OLD 30M budget) -> [1.9049 bigram regression] -> [v25 QK-norm build ERROR] -> **2.2969 (iter-19, FIRST at NEW committed 10M/384 budget — expected worse BPC, traded compute for ~6x speed)** -> **2.0549 (iter-20 v29, sweep-winner fold-in from GPU sweep 3sns1b3n, true-wood-14, 901s) — NEW BEST at the LOCKED budget. A SMALLER architecture (ch=2, d768, qdim64, chunk_ff 1024, local_window 64, token_dec 1/128, wd 0.1, clip 0.5) beats the previous d1024/ch4 config by 0.242 BPC under identical compute: finer chunk granularity + smaller upsampler is a real PerPos win, not compute inflation.**

vs_old_baseline_30m_bs96.interpretation: Expected regression: trading 24x fewer samples per epoch (3x fewer chars, 4x larger batch) for ~6x speed. Time-to-convergence target met (45 min saved), but BPC under-budget is the open problem. Architecture knobs (chunk_size, compressor design, lr range, sweep expansion incl chunk_size) are the only legitimate BPC levers now.

Iter-21 (v30) DIRECTION — keep EXHAUSTING the budget via sweep-winner rounds, one TPU push per sweep-wave, no compute inflation:

(a) Wait for GPU sweep 3sns1b3n (still draining, 7 kernels) to produce its next winner wave; fold into the canonical kernel via the ml-sweep-loop handoff. Do NOT push a random TPU config while the sweep is live — it duplicates the sweep agent's job.

(b) ch is now a CONFIG value (ch=2, moved out of FIXED in v29) — the next sweep wave should ALSO sweep ch in {1, 2, 4} on GPU to probe even finer granularity (ch=1 collapses to per-position; must stay AR-strict, verify coerce).
(c) lr range {6e-4, 9e-4, 1.2e-3} is already in the sweep space; consider extending to 1.8e-3 given only ~126 logged steps at bs384.

(e) Keep the tightened chunk_dec_dim_ff cap 2048->1024 (v29) — it matches the sweep winner and enforces a smaller chunk decoder (stronger hierarchy, anti-GPT-ification).

PRIMARY GOAL: EXHAUST THE BUDGET. Find the lowest BPC achievable at the locked 10M/512/256/bs384 budget (currently 2.0549). Every iteration must either improve BPC under this budget or justify the config on time-to-convergence — NEVER escape the budget by inflating compute.
